title: Gym and Fitness Studio HQ
description: For gyms: memberships, freezes, class capacity, PT packages, failed dues.

spec.useCase: The owner of Ironbark Fitness uses this to see who is active, frozen or leaving, which classes fill, which PT packages are running low and which dues failed.

business.name: Ironbark Fitness

pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour for the owner, the manager, the front desk and every coach. Read it once, then use the checklists at the bottom as your weekly rhythm.

A member's life in this workspace
Someone fills in the enquiry form or walks in. They become a

Book the free orientation within their first week. Members who get one stay far longer than members who are left to find their own way.

Replace the sample plans and prices with your own first, then the timetable and coaches. Delete the sample members once a dozen of your own are in. Health flags and emergency contacts are confidential: only staff who coach or run the desk should read them.
Members, classes, payments and requests at a glance. Review it every Monday.
Money not yet in (pending and failed)
Every member who asks to leave gets the same fair process: listen, log it, make one offer, respect the answer.

Most members who cancel were not unhappy with the gym. Their life changed: a new job, an injury, a trip, a tight month. A freeze or a cheaper plan keeps many of them, and the ones who still leave go with a good word for you. What loses members for good is a fight at the desk or a cancellation that takes three emails.
When a member asks to freeze
form and log it while they are in front of you. Pick the reason from the list; it feeds the reasons chart every quarter.
Check the plan's freeze fee and the member's minimum term. A freeze pauses the term: if they freeze for a month, the term ends a month later. Update
. Freezes run in whole months, one month minimum, three months maximum in a year unless it is medical.
Medical freezes with a doctor's note are free after the first month. Write it in the notes.

When a member asks to cancel
Ask why, and listen. Do not argue with the reason.

Check the notice period on their plan (30 days on monthly plans) and any minimum term left. Tell them the exact last day and the last payment, in writing.

What to look at each quarter
Requests by reason: if Cost leads, look at your off-peak price. If Not using it leads, look at orientations and first-month check-ins.
Members who cancelled within their first 90 days: did they get an orientation?
Words that help at the desk
Thanks for telling us. Can I ask what changed? ... We can pause it for a month or two instead, so your rate and your progress are waiting for you. If not, I'll make sure it's done properly today.
Never promise something only the manager can approve. Log it and say when they will hear back: the manager clears requests every morning.
Failed dues are the quietest way a gym loses money. Ten minutes every morning keeps most of it.

text.text: Send the message from the gym's phone, the same morning. Keep it short and human. Add one line to the payment notes saying what you sent.

Most failures clear on the first or second retry. After three failed attempts, the manager calls. If the member does not want to stay, that is a cancellation, not a debt chase: log the request and follow the cancellation steps. If they do want to stay, agree a date and set the next attempt for that day.

in the Next step column for anyone with a failed payment. When that member checks in, the desk says it quietly and privately: there is a problem with the card on file, can they update it now? Never at the counter in front of others, and never block entry on the first visit after a failure.
Do not add late fees on the first failure. It turns a missed card update into a reason to leave.
Do not retry a card every day; banks flag it.
Do not freeze a fob without the manager's say-so.
On the first Monday of the month, look at the

list on the Dashboard. Anything older than 30 days needs a decision from the manager: a payment plan, a cancellation, or writing it off. Write the decision into the payment's notes so nobody chases it twice.

Ask every new member for a card that will not expire in the next six months. When a member renews an annual plan, ask them to check the card on file at the same time. At the start of each month, filter the members whose cards expire this month and send one reminder before billing day.
A class that is always full is a signal to add a time. A class that runs at a third full for a month is a signal to move it.

Each coach is a member of the team. A coach who needs cover finds it from the coaches list, then changes the coach on that week's bookings, not on the timetable, unless the change is permanent. Coaches see their own sessions in
Members fill in health questions when they join. Anything flagged is written in

, which is confidential. Coaches read it before a member's first class and adjust: a lower box, a lighter bar, a different move. If a member says they have chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath during a class, stop them, sit them down, and call for help if it does not pass quickly.
Personal training is where a gym earns its margin and where members get results. Track every session so nobody runs out by surprise.
Most PT clients start with the
: a movement screen plus four sessions. It is a small yes and lets the coach and member see if they work well together.
Take payment in full before the first session. Add the payment with

Write the member's goal in their words, in one line. Every session should move toward it.
Each session is a booking linked to the package. When the member checks in,
goes down. No-shows and late cancels (under 24 hours for PT) use a session too, because the coach's hour is gone. Tell members this when they buy, and put it in writing.

column reads Offer the next package. The coach raises it in that session, not the last one: show the member what has changed since the first session (a weight, a time, a move they can now do) and offer the next package. Members who see their progress renew.

Packages expire so sessions do not sit unused for a year. The root page lists packages expiring in the next 30 days. A coach contacts each member with sessions left to book them in. If a member was ill or injured, the manager can extend the expiry once; write why in the package page.
